title: Integration discovery: gateway & observability with Galileo Systems
next_steps: SE to run 1-hour latency/throughput bench on our side and share results (Marcus)
Send security pack and SOC2 summary + KMS integration notes (Sophie)
Customer to share sample query distribution and current request rates (Daniel)
Schedule pilot kickoff for Dedicated eval w/ 2-week window
action_items: Marcus Lee — run preliminary latency benchmark (P95 token-gen) using 8k context, return CSV by 2027-07-22
Sophie Tran — send security artifacts (SOC2, ISO summary, KMS integration guide) and pricing sheet by 2027-07-16
Daniel Ortiz — provide sample traffic patterns and top-50 prompts, expected QPS and burst profile by 2027-07-20
summary: Discovery call focused on integration patterns (SDK + LangChain/LlamaIndex), gateway/proxy architecture, rate limits/quotas and observability hooks. Customer leaning toward a Dedicated pilot but needs clarity on VPC/private deployment, SSO/KMS, and routing/fallback behavior. Agreed next steps: bench, security docs, and pilot plan.
transcript:
[00:00] Sophie Tran: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Sophie from Redwood, AE on this account. Marcus (SE) and Aisha are with me. Could we quick intro on your side?
[00:12] Priya Kapoor: Yeah hi, I'm Priya, CTO at Galileo Systems. We've got Daniel, Elena and Tom here. Thanks for carving out time.
[00:20] Marcus Lee: Hey, Marcus here, SE — I'll mostly do the deep dive parts. Quick agenda: integration patterns, SDKs, gateway/proxy options, rate limits, and observability. Anything to add Priya?
[00:32] Priya Kapoor: That's good. We're evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for a chat summarization feature plus embeddings for search. Primary concerns are latency SLOs, data residency and key management.
[00:45] Daniel Ortiz: Yep and we use LangChain for orchestration and LlamaIndex in a couple of pipelines. We want to avoid wrapping too much custom infra.
[00:52] Sophie Tran: Great, thanks. Quick qualification — what are your current QPS and typical request sizes?
[00:59] Daniel Ortiz: Right now in staging maybe 6-8 rps, production spikes to maybe 120 rps during bulk indexing bursts. Prompts average 1.2k tokens, 8k context sometimes for long doc summarization.
[01:12] Elena Park: Infra notes: we run on GCP in a shared VPC, have a transit VPC for partners, and require customer-managed KMS for secrets in production.
[01:22] Tom Rivera: Timeline: we'd like a 2-week pilot then decide in 6 weeks. Budget constraints — prefer predictable unit costs, so Dedicated is attractive but need to see unit economics.
[01:35] Marcus Lee: Cool. On the SDK front — Redwood provides python and node SDKs, and a simple HTTP REST path. LangChain and LlamaIndex connectors: we have official adapters and also examples for using a gateway/proxy pattern if you want to centralize routing.
[01:50] Daniel Ortiz: Are the LangChain adapters upstream or maintained by you? We want long-term compatibility.
[01:55] Marcus Lee: Maintained by our integrations team, we land major changes into the LangChain/LL Writer ecosystems — sometimes the package names change, so we include pinned examples in our repo. They support streaming, function calls, and tool-calling.
[02:06] Priya Kapoor: Streaming is important. We need token-level billing visibility and per-call latencies for SLAs.
[02:12] Sophie Tran: Observability is a big part of Redwood Console: token-level cost breakdowns, per-model latency histograms, per-route dashboards, traces, and an exportable audit log for each request. You can push traces to your Datadog or Honeycomb.
[02:24] Elena Park: How do traces get emitted — do you instrument our app or do you get the request headers via gateway?
[02:29] Aisha Rahman: We support both. If you use the SDK, we inject tracing hooks and expose a trace-id header. If you run via a gateway or proxy, the gateway can propagate the headers. We also have a lightweight sidecar option that attaches to your service to emit enriched telemetry.
[02:43] Tom Rivera: Sidecar sounds interesting. But we worry about extra hops adding latency. How much overhead?
[02:48] Marcus Lee: The sidecar is local — it's not a network hop, more like a library process. Overhead is typically sub-5ms per request; depends on batching and length. For strict low-latency, many customers use SDK direct calls to Hosted or a Dedicated endpoint in the same region.
[03:03] Daniel Ortiz: About gateway vs proxy: we currently have an edge proxy (Envoy) in front of our services. We were thinking to funnel all LLM calls through a central gateway to control quotas and routing. Does Redwood support policy routing?
[03:16] Sophie Tran: Yes, policy routing is core: you can route by latency SLO, cost tier, region, or tenant. For example, during peak we route to a cheaper quantized model, or fallback to a different region. The gateway can enforce per-API-key quotas and rate limits.
[03:29] Priya Kapoor: If we route to cheaper models during peaks how do we monitor quality regressions? We can't have degraded summaries in prod.
[03:36] Marcus Lee: Great question — Redwood Optimize suggests model profiles for your workload, and you can tie quality monitors to a set of prompts/evals. When quality drops past a threshold, a rollback/fallback can trigger. We send regression alerts and allow canary rollouts.
[03:50] Elena Park: For private deployment — what parts live in our VPC? Do we have to open egress to Redwood control plane?
[03:58] Aisha Rahman: In Private mode the control plane is customer-managed in your VPC; the data path can be fully internal. For on-prem air-gapped, we package connectors and a local control plane. For VPC connectors we still optionally talk to Redwood for updates unless you choose isolated mode.
[04:12] Daniel Ortiz: KMS — can you integrate with our Google Cloud KMS or Hashicorp Vault? We need customer-managed keys for model inputs/outputs persistence.
[04:21] Marcus Lee: Yes, we integrate with GCP KMS, AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault and HashiVault. You can choose to encrypt persistent artifacts and also support HSM-based signing for audit logs.
[04:31] Tom Rivera: On quotas — we have different internal tenants (team A, team B). Can we set per-tenant budgets and soft/hard caps?
[04:38] Sophie Tran: Yes, per-API-key quotas with soft thresholds and alerts. You can also set token budgets per route and automatic throttling policies. For example soft-alert at 80% of daily budget then hard-block at 100% unless an override is applied.
[04:52] Priya Kapoor: On benchmarking — we'd like to see p50/p95/p99 latencies for your recommended Dedicated setup. Can you run a runbook for 8k context summarization?
[05:00] Marcus Lee: We can. Action item: we'll run a preliminary bench with an 8k context, simulate your burst profile, and share P50/P95/P99 plus cost per 1k tokens. We'll include both hosting and dedicated variants.
[05:12] Daniel Ortiz: For embeddings pipeline we have synchronous bulk runs and async streaming indexing — any guidance on batching?
[05:19] Aisha Rahman: For embeddings, batch sizes depend on GPU memory and quantization. Our recommendations: for FP16 models batch 64-128 on a single GPU. For quantized small models you can do bigger batch sizes; Redwood Optimize will analyze your payloads and recommend a batching profile.
[05:33] Elena Park: We use Prometheus + Grafana. Can Redwood export metrics to Prom or send traces to OTLP?
[05:39] Marcus Lee: Yes we emit Prom-compatible metrics and support OTLP and Zipkin. You can pull in per-route token counts, latency percentiles, cache hit rates, and billing tags.
[05:50] Priya Kapoor: About KV cache and prefix caching — our summarization heavily reuses context across sessions. Is prefix caching supported across nodes?
[05:58] Marcus Lee: We support KV cache sharding and a shared prefix cache. In Dedicated you can configure sticky routing so requests for the same conversation hit the same node and benefit from a hot KV cache. In Hosted mode we use a distributed cache and also smart routing to maintain affinity.
[06:14] Sophie Tran: Any security/regulatory constraints? Data residency?
[06:18] Priya Kapoor: Data residency: EU for EU customers, and for US we need SOC2 and audit trails. Also need SAML SSO integration and RBAC.
[06:26] Sophie Tran: Redwood has SOC2, SSO via SAML/OIDC, RBAC in Console, and detailed audit logs per token. We'll attach the security pack.
[06:33] Tom Rivera: Quick question about price model: Dedicated is a committed capacity plus per-token? Or flat?
[06:38] Sophie Tran: Dedicated is reserved GPU pools — you get committed throughput for a monthly fee and lower per-token runtime charge. There are burst credits for short peaks. Hosted is pure usage-based. We can model scenarios in a quick TCO sheet.
[06:50] Daniel Ortiz: We run LangChain chains that call into multiple tools. Is there function-calling support and structured outputs?
[06:56] Marcus Lee: Yes — function calling, structured output enforcers, schema validation hooks. The SDKs support streaming of tool outputs and partial sequences so you can interleave tool calls.
[07:05] Elena Park: Regarding proxy — if we put a gateway in our VPC that proxies to Redwood, do we lose some observability or billing granularity?
[07:13] Aisha Rahman: Not necessarily. If you propagate the trace headers and include the API key mapping, Console can still attribute costs per route/tenant. We recommend letting the gateway attach metadata headers (tenant-id, route-id).
[07:25] Priya Kapoor: Are there sandbox/playground credentials we can give to product folks?
[07:29] Sophie Tran: Yes, we can create team-level API keys and restricted keys for staging. We'll create a sandbox for your product team in the pilot.
[07:36] Tom Rivera: One concern: we use LlamaIndex heavy on our vector store; sometimes the library manages chunking differently — any gotchas?
[07:44] Marcus Lee: The common gotcha is inconsistent tokenization across chunking and model tokenizer. Our connectors include a tokenization check and recommended chunk sizes for each model family. We can share a small validation script.
[07:56] Daniel Ortiz: On the Dedicated side — how long to stand up? We need it within two weeks for the pilot.
[08:02] Sophie Tran: Typical provisioning is 3-7 business days for a standard Dedicated pool in an available region, faster if we have a partner pool. For VPC/private it can take longer — depends on network setup.
[08:13] Priya Kapoor: What's the fallback behavior if a node goes down mid-request?
[08:18] Marcus Lee: We have automatic request fallback to warm standby nodes and per-request progressive retry. For streamed responses we attempt reconnect semantics and return the partial chunk with an error code if irrecoverable.
[08:30] Elena Park: Do you support model pinning and gradual rollouts? We want to test a new quantized variant.
[08:36] Marcus Lee: Yes pin model versions per route, canary rollouts, A/B tests and automatic rollback if latency or eval metrics degrade.
[08:44] Sophie Tran: Quick check — what's the success criteria for this pilot?
[08:48] Priya Kapoor: Success: 1) Meet p95 latency < 250ms for 2k token prompts, 2) implement tenant quotas and cost tagging, 3) KMS integration working and SOC2 docs reviewed, 4) minimal infra changes.
[09:01] Marcus Lee: Noted. We'll design the bench to test those SLOs.
[09:06] Daniel Ortiz: For the bench, can you simulate our burst profile with 120 rps for 10-minute windows?
[09:12] Marcus Lee: Yes, include that in the bench. We'll include both Hosted and Dedicated runs.
[09:17] Tom Rivera: On observability hooks, will we be able to correlate model tokens to user ids in our system?
[09:22] Aisha Rahman: Yes, pass a user-id header and Console will index by that tag. We also support custom tags to slice cost.
[09:30] Priya Kapoor: Are there any limitations on request size for streaming with function calls?
[09:34] Marcus Lee: Streaming supports up to the model max context — practical limits depend on memory. For Dedicated we can allocate larger sequence handlers and tuned kernels for 32k contexts in certain model families.
[09:47] Sophie Tran: I'll note the pilot design items. Any blockers today?
[09:51] Elena Park: Only KMS and network egress policies — we need to review the security pack.
[09:56] Sophie Tran: We'll send it after the call.
[09:59] Priya Kapoor: Good. Also want SLA terms for Dedicated and a draft contract.
[10:04] Sophie Tran: We'll include the SLA summary and draft MSA.
[10:08] Marcus Lee: One last technical note — for LangChain/LlamaIndex we recommend using the SDK not raw HTTP for better retry semantics and streaming; connectors will handle tokenization and chunking.
[10:19] Daniel Ortiz: Makes sense. We may need help modifying our LangChain chains to use the Redwood connector. Can SE assist in a workshop?
[10:26] Marcus Lee: Yes, we can do a 90-min workshop as part of the pilot.
[10:30] Tom Rivera: Ok great.
[10:31] Sophie Tran: Recap of next steps — Marcus will run bench, Sophie will send security & pricing, Daniel will share traffic patterns, and we'll schedule pilot kickoff. We'll follow up with a calendar invite.
[10:43] Priya Kapoor: Thanks all, talk soon.
[10:46] Sophie Tran: Thanks everyone, bye.
[10:50] (call ends)
